G.5-2.label: Parallel Line Angles
G.5-2.example: ∠4 and ∠6 are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary: 70° + 110° = 180°.

G.5-4.label: Exterior Angles
G.5-4.example: Remote interior angles 38° and 81°, so the exterior angle = 38° + 81° = 119°.

G.5-5.label: AA Similarity
G.5-5.example: △ABC has 32° and 104°, so ∠C = 44°. △XYZ has 104° and 44°: similar by AA.

G.5-7.label: Error Analysis
G.5-7.example: Same-side angles add to 180°, not equal: (5x − 20) + (3x + 40) = 180, x = 20.

G.5-8.label: Mathematical Justification
G.5-8.example: Draw a line through the top parallel to the base: alternate interior angles match, filling a straight line (180°).

G.6-1.label: Legs & Hypotenuse
G.6-1.example: Legs 20 and 21; hypotenuse 29 is longest, across from the right angle: 20² + 21² = 29².

G.6-2.label: Area of Squares
G.6-2.example: Squares on the legs: 25 cm² + 144 cm² = 169 cm², the square on the hypotenuse.

G.6-3.label: The Converse
G.6-3.example: 33² + 56² = 65², so the triangle is a right triangle.

G.6-4.label: Testing Side Lengths
G.6-4.example: 9, 40, 41: 81 + 1,600 = 1,681 = 41², so it is a right triangle.

G.6-5.label: Area Model Explanation
G.6-5.example: Big square 23² − 4 triangles (240) = 289 = c², and 8² + 15² = 289 too.

G.6-6.label: Justifying Right Angles
G.6-6.example: 16² + 30² = 1,156 but 37² = 1,369, so the corner is not a right angle.

G.6-7.label: Error Analysis
G.6-7.example: Wrong: 7² + 25² = 24². Fix: c is longest, so 7² + 24² = 25²: it is right.

G.6-8.label: Conceptual Proof
G.6-8.example: Big square (a + b)² minus 4 triangles of area ab/2 leaves a² + b², the tilted square c².

G.6-9.label: Theorem vs. Converse
G.6-9.example: Find a missing side: use the theorem. Check if a corner is 90°: use the converse.

G.7-1.label: Legs & Hypotenuse
G.7-1.example: Right angle at Q, legs PQ = 9 and QR = 40: hypotenuse PR = 41.

G.7-2.label: Right Triangles Only
G.7-2.example: A triangle with an 80° angle and no 90° angle: a² + b² = c² does not apply.

G.7-3.label: Find a Missing Side
G.7-3.example: 25-ft wire, stake 7 ft away: h² = 625 − 49 = 576, so h = 24 ft.

G.7-5.label: Word Problem Diagrams
G.7-5.example: 17-ft ladder, base 8 ft out: draw it, 8² + h² = 17², h = 15 ft.

G.7-6.label: Radical Side Lengths
G.7-6.example: Hypotenuse √97, leg 4: 97 − 16 = 81, so the other leg is 9.

G.7-7.label: 3D & Multi-Step
G.7-7.example: Box 16 × 12 × 15 in: floor diagonal 20 in, corner to corner √(20² + 15²) = 25 in.

G.7-8.label: Simplifying Radicals
G.7-8.example: Rope 9 ft, stake 3 ft away: h = √(81 − 9) = √72 = 6√2 ft.

G.8-1.label: Horizontal & Vertical Distance
G.8-1.example: (−3, −2) to (5, 4): 8 units across and 6 units up.

G.8-2.label: Build a Right Triangle
G.8-2.example: A(−4, −1), B(4, 5): corner C(4, −1), legs 8 and 6, AB is the hypotenuse.

G.2-1.label: Three Rigid Motions
G.2-1.example: A translation slides, a reflection flips over a line, a rotation turns around a point.

G.2-2.label: Graph One Move
G.2-2.example: Reflect (−4, 2) across the x-axis → (−4, −2); do this for each vertex and plot.

G.2-3.label: Size & Shape Stay
G.2-3.example: GH = 7 cm, ∠I = 70°; after a rotation, G′H′ = 7 cm, ∠I′ = 70°.

G.2-4.label: Congruent Parts
G.2-4.example: A y-axis reflection maps △ABC onto △DEF, so they are congruent and BC matches EF.

G.2-6.label: Missing Sides
G.2-6.example: AB = WX in congruent figures: 3x + 2 = 17, so x = 5.

G.2-7.label: Congruence Proof
G.2-7.example: A reflection then a translation maps △TUV onto △KLM; both are rigid, so △TUV ≅ △KLM.

G.2-8.label: Most Efficient Moves
G.2-8.example: Reflect over the x-axis, then y-axis = one 180° turn; the one-step turn is best.

G.2-9.label: Congruent vs. Similar
G.2-9.example: Rigid moves give congruent figures; adding a dilation gives similar, not congruent, figures.

G.4-1.label: Dilation Basics
G.4-1.example: Dilate by 1.5: side 6 → 9, and a 90° angle stays 90°.

G.4-3.label: Testing Similarity
G.4-3.example: 6/4 = 1.5 and 15/10 = 1.5, and all angles are 90°, so the rectangles are similar.

G.4-5.label: Sequences with Dilation
G.4-5.example: (4, 6): dilate by 1/2 → (2, 3), reflect over the y-axis → (−2, 3).

G.4-6.label: Congruent, Similar, or Neither
G.4-6.example: Translate, then rotate: congruent. Dilate by 4, then translate: similar, not congruent.

G.4-8.label: Similarity Proof
G.4-8.example: Dilate by 3, then rotate 90°: △ABC lands on △DEF; angles stay, sides ×3, so similar.

G.4-9.label: Indirect Measurement
G.4-9.example: Same sun angle and 90° ground make similar triangles: 5/4 = h/36, so the tree is 45 ft.

G.3-1.label: Rigid vs. Non-Rigid
G.3-1.example: A dilation by 2 changes the size, so it is non-rigid; the image is similar, not congruent.

G.3-5.label: Finding Scale Factor
G.3-5.example: AB = 4 → A′B′ = 6, AC = 3 → A′C′ = 4.5: k = 1.5 both times.

G.3-7.label: Error Analysis
G.3-7.example: (2, 5) rotated 90° clockwise is (5, −2), not (−5, 2); that is the counterclockwise rule.

G.3-8.label: Combined Moves
G.3-8.example: Rotate 180°, then dilate by 2: (x, y) → (−2x, −2y); similar, not congruent.

G.3-9.label: Scale Factor & Area
G.3-9.example: Dilate by 3: sides ×3 and area ×9 (12 → 108); same angles, so similar, not congruent.

G.9-1.label: Radius, Diameter, Height
G.9-1.example: Can with diameter 8 cm and height 11 cm: r = 4 cm, h = 11 cm.

G.9-2.label: Cylinder Volume
G.9-2.example: r = 3 cm, h = 8 cm: V = π(3²)(8) = 72π cm³.

G.9-6.label: Cone & Sphere Fractions
G.9-6.example: Cylinder holds 432π cm³, so the matching cone holds 144π and the sphere 288π cm³.

G.9-7.label: Real-World & Errors
G.9-7.example: Cone d = 12 in, h = 10 in: use r = 6, not 12, so V = 120π in³.

G.9-8.label: Missing Radius or Height
G.9-8.example: Cone 48π ft³, h = 9: (1/3)πr²(9) = 48π, r² = 16, r = 4 ft.

G.9-9.label: Composite Solids
G.9-9.example: Cylinder π(3²)(20) = 180π plus cone (1/3)π(3²)(4) = 12π: total 192π cm³.

G.9-10.label: Scaling Volume
G.9-10.example: Triple r: volume ×9, because r is squared. Triple h: volume only ×3.
